extra.message: req.body is passed directly to node-serialize's unserialize(). node-serialize is a well-known RCE vector: a payload like {"rce":"_$$ND_FUNC$$_function(){require('child_process').exec('id')}()"} is executed as JS when unserialize() parses it. The route is only gated by authenticateToken, so any authenticated (even low-privilege) user can achieve remote code execution on the server.

The '/secret/' route takes an attacker-controlled 'url' query parameter (request.query['url']) and passes it unvalidated to needle.get(url), then reflects the response body back to the client. This allows Server-Side Request Forgery: an attacker can make the server issue requests to internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, http://localhost:<internal-port>/) and read back the response.

userSchema.findOne() is called with req.body.username and req.body.password inserted directly as query operands. Because body-parser's urlencoded parser (extended:true) parses bracket syntax into nested objects (e.g. password[$ne]=1), an attacker can submit username=admin&password[$ne]=null to make MongoDB match on '$ne' rather than an exact password, bypassing authentication (NoSQL injection / auth bypass).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: req.query.user is passed directly as the value of 'username' in userSchema.findOne(). Express's default query parser (qs) turns bracket syntax like ?user[$ne]=null into an object, letting an attacker inject MongoDB operators (e.g. $ne, $regex) to match arbitrary/all user documents.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: POST /secret/?user has no authentication middleware and returns the full raw Mongoose user document (res.json(result)) — including the plaintext 'password' and 'admin' fields — for any username supplied via query string. Any unauthenticated caller can dump another user's credentials.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: POST /secret/username has no authentication middleware and returns the full raw user document (res.json(result)) for any username supplied in the body — exposing plaintext passwords and the admin flag of any account to unauthenticated callers.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: During signup, the 'admin' field of the new user document is set directly from req.body.admin (the code even comments '// privilege escalation'). A registrant can POST admin=true to /secret/signup and immediately create an administrator account, bypassing any privilege restriction.

GET /secret/posts/:username fetches posts for the :username route parameter, then only checks that the JWT payload has a (truthy) username at all — it never compares payload.username to req.params.username (marked '// broken access control' in the source). Any authenticated user can view any other user's posts by changing the URL parameter.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The JWT signing secret is a hardcoded, low-entropy string ('hello') used to sign both the session access token and the password-reset token. Anyone with access to the source (or who guesses/brute-forces it) can forge valid tokens for any username, including admin:true, granting full authentication bypass and account takeover.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: express-session is configured with a hardcoded secret ('Your_Secret_Key'), allowing forgery of session cookies if the source is exposed.

req.body.password is stored on the new user document as-is with no hashing (e.g. bcrypt). The user schema (models/user.js) also declares 'password' with no type/hashing hook. Combined with the login route comparing plaintext passwords directly in the DB query, this means all credentials are stored and compared in cleartext, and a DB compromise exposes every user's real password.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: csurf middleware is instantiated ('csrfProtection') but never applied to any router, and app.js:103 shows the equivalent middleware commented out. None of the state-changing POST routes (signup, login, forgot-password, addpost, password-reset, shell) enforce a CSRF token, so all of them are exploitable via cross-site request forgery from an attacker-controlled page while the victim's session/JWT cookie is active.

jwt.sign() is called with no 'expiresIn' option for the login access token (and again at line 522 for the password-reset token), so both tokens are valid forever. A leaked/stolen Auth cookie or reset link therefore grants indefinite access/reset capability with no way to force expiry short of rotating the shared secret.

The forgot-password handler returns a distinct message ('Email Address is not associated with account') when the email is not found versus a generic success message when it is, letting an attacker enumerate which email addresses have registered accounts (already flagged '// User enumeration' in the source).

The authentication JWT (req.cookies.Auth) is printed to server logs. Elsewhere the raw login credentials (username+password, line 138) and the unsigned reset token (line 525) are also logged. If logs are aggregated/shipped to a third party or are otherwise accessible, this exposes session tokens and plaintext passwords.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The /auth/callback route accepts a bearer 'token' supplied directly by the client and forwards it to Google's userinfo endpoint to authenticate the user, without verifying the token's audience/client_id belongs to this application. A token minted for any other Google OAuth client (which an attacker may legitimately possess) will be accepted here, letting an attacker authenticate as themselves under this app's session using a token never intended for it (audience-confusion).

app.use(blinker(basePath, [{ test: /.*/  ... }])) serves the 'images' directory via the express-blinker package, which is explicitly annotated in the source as '//directory traversal'. The catch-all regex test (/.*/) applies the static handler to every request path with no additional sanitization layered on top, relying entirely on the third-party package to prevent '../' traversal outside of the images directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Gmail account credentials (USER/PASS) for the application's mail sender are hardcoded in a committed config file, and utils/sendemail.js:10-16 duplicates the hardcoded account address inline in the nodemailer transport config.
